data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'kahatibah' meaning 'speaker' or 'orator'. In Islamic tradition, a Khatib is a person who delivers the Friday sermon (Khutbah) in a mosque. The name Khatiba carries the meaning “Speaker, Orator” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Khatiba usually hope their child will grow to embody speaker, orator and live with faith, good character and purpose.

Distinctive styles and oratorical techniques have emerged over centuries, reflecting the rich cultural heritage and diversity of the Islamic world.
